subject: AcmeHealth Private VPC data flow review and next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alice Morgan <alice.morgan@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-08-04T16:12:00-07:00
Subject: AcmeHealth Private VPC data flow review and next steps

Hi Alice - great speaking with you and Bob earlier today. Quick recap from our discovery and the open items we discussed: 

- Scope: Platform will serve embeddings + generation for care triage workflows. You flagged PII and PHI as in-scope for the triage path.
- Data residency: primary requirement is to host in us-west-2; some workflows may require on-prem/air-gapped handling.
- Retention & logging: target audit log retention = 365 days; need controls for redaction/pseudonymization for downstream analytics.
- Network: preferred pattern is a customer-managed VPC peering/privatelink with no public egress for request payloads; also discussed outbound egress controls and approved IP ranges.

Attachments: redwood_private_vpc_diagram.pdf (draft architecture), acme_vpc_requirements.xlsx (we sketched mapping to your checklist).

Next steps / asks: 
1) Confirm whether any additional internal stakeholders should join the VPC architecture review (we recommend your network/security and platform engineering).
2) Confirm the list of data types that must never leave your environment in plaintext (PHI, SSNs, etc.).
3) Proposed times for a 60-min architecture review next week: Tue 8/10 9-11am PT or Wed 8/11 10am-12pm PT.

We'll have Neha (security lead) and Rishi (solutions engineering) join to walk the diagram and answer the egress/encryption questions.

Thanks,

Marissa Cole
Enterprise Solutions
Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com

Hi Marissa,

Thanks for the recap - that matches our notes. A few clarifications from our side: 

- We do handle PHI for triage; anything that identifies a patient must remain in our control. We can provide a classification mapping (PDF attached).
- Primary cloud region should be us-west-2; we may require an on-prem gateway for a small subset of sensitive workflows (legal/forensic).
- Audit/log retention requirement: 365 days is our preference, with the ability to export to our SIEM.

I'm looping in Bob (platform) and Vivek from your team. Please include your security lead.

Available for the architecture call: Tue 8/10 09:30-10:30 PT works for me.

Best,

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alice Morgan <alice.morgan@acmehealth.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-08-05T10:30:00-07:00
Subject: RE: AcmeHealth Private VPC data flow review and next steps

Hi Alice / team - I'm Neha from Redwood security. A few items I want to surface ahead of the architecture review so we can make the meeting actionable: 

1) Data classification & flow: please confirm which payloads contain PHI vs. non-PII. We need to know which endpoints must never traverse public networks.
2) Encryption: all in-transit traffic must be TLS1.2+; for data-at-rest we recommend customer-managed KMS keys (bring-your-own-key) for the private deployment.
3) Egress controls: confirm if you require zero-egress (no outbound internet access) for certain workloads; if so, we'll scope an on-prem gateway or air-gapped packaging.
4) Logging & retention: we can provide audit logs for request/response metadata; sensitive payloads can be redacted prior to storage. What level of detail do you need in logs (full request, metadata-only)?
5) Key management & access: will you be using your own KMS/HSM? We support AWS KMS and customer HSM integrations for Private.

Attachments: soc2-summary.pdf (Redwood SOC 2 in-scope controls).

If you can answer 1-3 before the call, we'll tailor the diagram to show which components touch plaintext PII and options for segregating them.

Thanks,

Neha Kapoor
Head of Security & Compliance, Product
Redwood Inference
neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com

From: Alice Morgan <alice.morgan@acmehealth.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Bob Chen <bob.chen@acmehealth.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-08-06T12:15:00-07:00
Subject: Re: AcmeHealth Private VPC data flow review and next steps

Hi Neha / Marissa,

Answers below: 
- Data: triage payloads include PHI (patient name, DOB, limited clinical notes). Non-PII telemetry is separate.
- Zero-egress: for legal/forensic workflows we do expect zero public egress. Regular triage workloads can have restricted outbound to approved endpoints only.
- KMS: we will provide our own AWS KMS keys; would like to integrate with your private deployment.
- Logs: metadata-only in the platform is preferred; full request bodies should be redacted and available only via secure export on demand.

We are targeting a compliance sign-off by end of Q3. If you can show an on-prem/air-gapped option in the diagram that would be critical.

Available for the 8/10 09:30 PT call.

Best,

Alice Morgan
Head of Security & Compliance
AcmeHealth
Attachment: acme_data_classification.pdf

Thanks everyone - confirmed for Tue 8/10, 09:30-10:30 PT. Calendar invite with dial-in going out now (link: https://calendar.google.com/event?eid=acme-vpc-arch-review).

What we'll cover in the architecture review: 
- VPC/private deployment topology (peering vs. privatelink) and where payloads are decrypted
- KMS integration and BYOK flow for keys
- Egress controls and options for zero-egress / on-prem gateway
- Logging model: metadata-first with redaction workflows and secure export for full payloads
- Operational SLAs and handoff for forensic/on-prem transfers

Pre-read: redwood_private_vpc_diagram.pdf (draft) - we'll update it before the call to include the on-prem gateway flow you requested.

Thanks - looking forward to the review.
